HEADLINE: Charles Schwab: The Schwab Trading Activity Index (STAX) decreased to 48.48 in December, down from its score of 48.75 in November

During the December STAX period, which ended on the 26th of the month, the STAX broke a three-month streak of outpacing the S&P 500 index, which itself only rose 1.18%. Clients were net sellers during the period, but movement within the STAX Index was minimal, with much of the selling occurring during the holiday-shortened final week and more likely to represent end-of-year repositioning activity than a major sentiment change. At the sector level, Information Technology went from the largest net-buy in November to biggest net-sell in December, while Consumer Discretionary saw the second-most net selling, followed by Health Care, Industrials, and Energy. Major U.S. indexes set all-time highs on December 26, the very end of the STAX period, but those new heights represented just a slight increase from both earlier in the month and the previous highs set back in October. December saw a widely-anticipated rate cut from the Federal Reserve-its third since September-and a surprisingly strong third quarter gross domestic product growth figure alongside a softer-than-expected Consumer Price Index for November. The most aggressively positioned investors tracked by Schwab during December again belonged to Generation X, born between 1965 and 1980. (AVGO) Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) Names net sold by Schwab clients during the period included: Tesla Inc. (TSLA) Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) Intel Corp. </article>

<summary>
Schwab's STAX index dipped slightly to 48.48 in December from 48.75 in November, ending a three-month streak of outperforming the S&P 500 (+1.18%). Client selling was modest and concentrated in the holiday-shortened final week, suggesting year-end repositioning rather than sentiment shift. Tech flipped from top net-buy sector to top net-sell, followed by Consumer Discretionary, Health Care, Industrials, and Energy. Markets hit fresh highs late in the period amid a third Fed rate cut, strong Q3 GDP, and cooler CPI data. Gen X remained most aggressively positioned; Gen Z least. </summary>
